witness.name: Delphi.CellGeometry.tripleJunction_120_witness
witness.statement: theorem tripleJunction_120_witness : ∃ u v w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ ‖v‖ = 1 ∧ ‖w‖ = 1 ∧ junctionBalanced 1 1 1 u v w

joint.outcome: theorem from standard axioms with no shared-scope hypotheses: consistent with every satisfiable law set

law.label: Plateau's first rule: three equal-tension walls meet at 120 degrees
law.statement_en: Where three fluid walls of the same positive tension meet at a point and balance, every pair of walls meets at exactly 120 degrees; the sizes of the cells on either side never enter. Stated in any real inner-product space, so it covers both cell walls seen in section and soap films meeting along an edge in three dimensions.

hypotheses.name: plateau-triple-junction-120#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: The walls are fluid films of uniform tension in static equilibrium: the junction condition is the vector sum of the three tensions along the wall directions being zero (Neumann's triangle). Nothing is said about how a tissue reaches equilibrium or whether a given epithelium is one.

hypotheses.name: plateau-triple-junction-120#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Equal tension on all three walls. With unequal tensions the angles follow junction_inner (T3^2 = T1^2 + T2^2 + 2 T1 T2 cos angle) and are not 120 degrees.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model of fluid walls under tension; it applies wherever the walls are such films and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: Exact: T•u + T•v + T•w = 0 with unit u, v, w and T > 0 gives angle(u,v) = angle(v,w) = angle(u,w) = 2π/3 (tripleJunction_120).
General Neumann triangle: T3^2 = T1^2 + T2^2 + 2 T1 T2 <u,v> (junction_inner).
Non-vacuity: the unit vectors at 0, 120 and 240 degrees in the plane are balanced under equal tension (tripleJunction_120_witness).
assumed: Fluid walls of uniform tension in static equilibrium (force balance at the junction is the whole model).
Equal tension on all three walls.

sources: On Growth and Form (1917), chapter VII (claim thompson1917-ch07-04; Lean port of ThompsonLaws.Cells.tripleJunction_120)
Plateau, Statique expérimentale et théorique des liquides soumis aux seules forces moléculaires (1873), first rule
On Growth and Form (1917), chapter VII (claim thompson1917-ch07-04)
